day.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
day.readme: Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. day.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
day.readme: A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting. This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness. The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

day.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
day.readme: My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.

day.readme: An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now: by people and the agents working alongside them. Currently in Beta · Built on React 19+ and StyleX Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company, powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day.

NVIDIA Kubernetes® Engine (NVKE) provides the management plane that platform teams install to create and operate Kubernetes clusters for their customers. Each workload cluster has its own Kubernetes control plane, etcd and node pools. You operate the NVKE management plane; your customers use their clusters through the Kubernetes API and kubectl.

week.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
week.readme: Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it. Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together. Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents.

week.description: Worktrunk is a CLI for Git worktree management, designed for parallel AI agent workflows
week.readme: Worktrunk is a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel. Worktrunk's three core commands make worktrees as easy as branches. Plus, Worktrunk has a bunch of quality-of-life features to simplify working with many parallel changes, including hooks to automate local workflows & copy-on-write build caches. AI agents like Claude Code and Codex can handle longer tasks without supervision, such that it's possible to manage 5-10+ in parallel.

week.description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio, 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.
week.readme: Turn a single Claude Code session into a full game development studio. 49 agents. 74 skills. One coordinated AI team. Building a game solo with AI is powerful, but a single chat session has no structure. No one stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping design docs, or writing spaghetti code. There's no QA pass, no design review, no one asking "does this actually fit the game's vision?" Claude Code Game Studios solves this by giving your AI session the structure of a real studio.

Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

week.description: Hyprland is an independent, highly customizable, dynamic tiling Wayland compositor that doesn't sacrifice on its looks.
week.readme: Hyprland is a 100% independent, dynamic tiling Wayland compositor that doesn't sacrifice on its looks. It provides the latest Wayland features, is highly customizable, has all the eyecandy, the most powerful plugins, easy IPC, much more QoL stuff than other compositors and more... [ Quick Start ][Quick Start] [ Contribute ][Contribute] All of the eyecandy: gradient borders, many types of blur, animations, glow, shadows and much more 100% independent, no wlroots, no libweston, no kwin, no mutter.

week.description: 💫 Toolkit to help you get started with SDD or any other process!
week.readme: Build with a spec, fix a bug, or assess an idea, with your coding agent. Spec Kit is an open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes. Start with a ready-made process, customize it, or bring your own. These are independent entry points, not mandatory phases. SDD ships in core; bug fixing and assessment are bundled extensions you install when needed, and the primitives below let you adopt or create other processes.

week.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
week.readme: Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them. It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

week.description: 🚀 PR Agent: The Original Open-Source PR Reviewer. This project is not the Qodo free tier.
week.readme: The Original Open-Source PR Reviewer This repository contains the open-source PR Agent Project. It is not the Qodo offering for open-source projects. PR-Agent is an open-source, AI-powered code review agent and a community-maintained legacy project of Qodo. It is distinct from Qodo's primary AI code review offering, which provides a feature-rich, context-aware experience.

week.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.
week.readme: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, and catch AI slop before it ships. Reload your coding tool, then run /impeccable init in your agent ($impeccable init on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs.

week.description: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
week.readme: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets 🚩 [2025.11.10] Kronos has been accpeted by AAAI 2026. 🚩 [2025.08.17] We have released the scripts for fine-tuning! Check them out to adapt Kronos to your own tasks. 🚩 [2025.08.02] Our paper is now available on arXiv! Kronos is a family of decoder-only foundation models, pre-trained specifically for the "language" of financial markets, K-line sequences.

month.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
month.readme: See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level. Join the Reverse Engineering Community See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites.

month.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
month.readme: A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated. Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of fifty materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an...

month.description: ArtCraft is an intentional crafting engine for artists, designers, and filmmakers
month.readme: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7339bd09-3e0d-44a7-a024-af9de64e4c11 Watch the two-minute ArtCraft demo on YouTube ArtCraft is the IDE for interactive AI image and video creation. Compose in 2D, stage scenes in 3D, and choose the models that fit your work. Turn prompting into crafting with visual tools for precise, repeatable results. Artists need control over composition, character identity, and camera placement. Build the scene before you generate it. Click any preview to view it at full size.

month.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
month.readme: A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting. This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness. The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

month.description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
month.readme: Tool for automatic executables porting to Linux and Windows. The relinker-only build runs on macOS, including Apple silicon. Web converter - files stay on your device. Includes a relinker that converts executable to the target system's native format and implementations of system prx libraries suitable for dynamic linking. No emulation or separate runtime process.

month.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative, voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.
month.readme: 🎉 100,000 GitHub stars, thank you! AI voice studio. On your device. Clone, design, dub, dictate, transcribe and narrate in 646 languages. Runs on your laptop, desktop, servers, phone, tablets and more Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice. Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original. Describe a voice in words and generate it. Choose your engines and download only the models you need.

month.description: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.
month.readme: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents. HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The HyperFrames Studio app is free to use as well; its Pro plan adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent?

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app (iOS, Android), web app and Electron-based desktop app. Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them. Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents.

month.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
month.readme: Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it. Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together. Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents.

new.description: Craft Anything: understand how any software works, and craft your own.
new.readme: See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust. Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools, has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it. A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

new.description: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
new.readme: dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person. It is also a way of working with an agent: take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.

new.description: VERY experimental Nintendo Switch 2 emulator
new.readme: Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. Visit the official Lichii website to find games and compare community compatibility reports. Download Lichii only from this repository's releases page.

new.description: 244 pixel art effects, every one a small piece of code. Plus a Claude Code skill to make your own.
new.readme: 244 pixel art effects and animations, every one a small piece of code. Fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters and more. Play them live, recolor and mirror them, drop them into a browser game, or export sprite sheets for any engine. Plus a Claude Code skill that makes new ones the way a picky pixel artist would: draft, render, look, refine. Every effect that involves a character is acted out: he winds up, lets go, freezes on contact and recovers, and a target takes the hit.

new.description: A Claude Code skill that turns any machine into a 3D simulator you can take apart
new.readme: A Claude Code skill that turns any machine into a 3D simulator you can take apart. Ask how something works. Claude builds it as one offline HTML page: the machine runs in the middle, every panel around it reads the real numbers, a button opens the part doing the work, and when nobody touches it the page tours itself. new.description: Free Claude skill: viral animated story shorts (2D characters in a 3D world) with three.js + Remotion
new.readme: The free Claude skill from the video "How to Make Viral Animated Shorts Using Claude (Full Workflow)". It makes 55-70 s vertical animated story shorts: 2D characters in a colourful 3D world, with ink outlines, a painted town, lens blur, gliding cameras, a march score and sound effects. Everything is rendered with three.js inside Remotion on your own PC, with no AI video generator. Proven on The Bridge That Fell for a Song, a 67 s short about the 1831 Broughton bridge.

new.description: Entire MacOS running in your terminal.
new.readme: A separate macOS desktop for computer-use agents, viewed and controlled from a terminal. terminal-mac is an early release candidate for Apple silicon. Apple Virtualization runs a real macOS guest. A bundled helper inside that guest captures its screen and posts input events. A terminal viewer streams that screen using Kitty or iTerm2 graphics. Agent commands use the same helper without moving the physical Mac's pointer or changing its clipboard.

new.description: A Native Recompilation Of The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Nintendo Switch 2 Remake
new.readme: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator. Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows program, the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game. Discord: https://discord.gg/DVQQJphbBf Experimental.

new.description: Agent skill: describe your stack in a sentence, get an architecture diagram with official logos
new.readme: Describe your stack in a sentence. Get an architecture diagram with official logos. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other agents that support skills. In the Claude apps, upload stack-diagram.zip from Releases as a skill. Draw our monorepo tooling: a pnpm workspace with Turborepo, Biome, Vitest and Lefthook. GitHub Actions runs CI and publishes to npm. Draw our docs chatbot: Next.js on Vercel searches Supabase pgvector and answers with Claude. Inngest syncs Notion every night.

new.description: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick
new.readme: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick. hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install Downloads from official sources. It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. Makes room safely.

new.description: Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LuaLaTeX, with plants and visitors sampled from genomes and a TikZ library that also draws them under pdfLaTeX
new.readme: Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LaTeX. No images, no imported paths, no external assets: every petal, leaf and stem is a curve computed while the page is being written, painted like a watercolor, and written straight into the PDF. Every page grows a garden of its own, and each document's seed its own plants, each sampled from a genome. Six seeds of the grown margin.

new.description: Blazing-fast native notes app for macOS & Windows. Rust + GPUI, local-first, compatible with Feishu/Lark DocxXML.
new.readme: A fast, quiet, local notes app. Drawn natively with Rust + GPUI. Your notes stay on your computer, stored in the Feishu (Lark) DocxXML format. ⚡ Fast, the native kind of fast. The whole interface is drawn on the GPU by Rust and GPUI. No WebView, no Electron. In a one-million-character document, typing, deleting and scrolling all stay under 6 ms per frame at P95. 🔒 Local-first. Your files are yours. No account, no cloud, and nothing goes over the network by default (the optional update check aside).

new.readme: A tiny, fast container runtime for macOS, Windows and Linux. Runs your Docker images and works with the docker CLI, Compose and buildx you already use. Kiri is a lightweight replacement for Docker Desktop and OrbStack, written in Rust. It runs containers in one small Linux VM (or straight on the kernel on Linux) and speaks the Docker Engine API, so your tools just work. The name comes from the Igbo word ntakịrị, "small". Fast: a container starts and exits in about 2.5 ms through the Docker API.

new.description: A research prototype for zero-knowledge proofs of AI inference. Not maintained.
new.readme: FlashProve lets an AI provider prove which model answered a request, without revealing the model's Commit. The provider publishes a commitment ID, which binds it to one set of weights. The weights themselves stay secret: every published value that depends on them is masked, except a declared list. Prove. For each reply, the provider's GPU produces a proof that the reply is the committed Verify.

new.description: Emulate macOS on iOS and iPadOS
new.readme: Download macOS, install it on the device, and use it. Own emulator, iOS gives apps no hypervisor, so Henge runs the Mac's arm64 code through its own JIT, with its own MMU and devices. It doesn't use QEMU or Virtualization.framework. Installs on the device, Henge downloads Apple's restore image and restores it the way a Mac does. No Mac needed, and nothing is decrypted or patched. Graphics, macOS draws through a virtual GPU, and Henge replays its commands with Metal.

items.title: GitHub admins can push a persisted-approval secret check to every repo in one script
items.connection: The Claude Code leak shows what to look for, the Copilot review API lets admins set review policy from enterprise down to repo, and the Cloudflare audit skill emits machine-readable findings that can feed that review.
items.context: most enterprises roll out coding agents faster than security can review each repo by hand
chain: A vendor scan reports passwords from a "Don't Ask Again" approval shortcut in 1,122 public GitHub files.
Copilot code review settings can now be scripted through APIs, so a platform team can enable review on every repo at once instead of clicking through settings.
Audit findings in a machine-readable format can be checked against the same repos, so persisted-approval files become one more pattern reviewers are pointed at.
Security teams get a repeatable rollout they can rerun whenever a new agent shortcut causes leaks, which turns a one-off incident into a standing control.
items.who: Platform and AppSec teams at firms with many GitHub repos benefit; the CISO budget pays.
items.variable: time from leak disclosure to org-wide coverage
items.versus: Clicking through settings repo by repo takes weeks, and a generic secret scanner is not tuned to the files agent approvals write.
items.smallest_test: Script review settings across 20 internal repos, seed 10 with fake credentials in agent approval files, and count it a success if at least 8 are flagged before merge.
items.disconfirm: Review and audit together flag fewer seeded approval-file secrets than an existing secret scanner already does.

items.connection: MaxxBench shows small task edits spread models tied near 74% by up to 23 points, and Nanbeige4.3-33B's 80.9 versus 73.0 lead is maker-reported on a single headline benchmark.
items.context: procurement teams usually shortlist models by public leaderboard scores
chain: Nanbeige reports 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 against 73.0 for Qwen3.8-27B, a gap that looks decisive for an in-house pick.
MaxxBench shows models tied on headline scores can differ by up to 23 points once tasks are lightly edited, so instruction following decides real fit.
Thinking Inertia metrics add a second check: whether the model obeys no-thinking modes that teams rely on for cost.
Consultants can sell a short model bake-off on the client's own edited tasks, which prevents a costly wrong standardization.
items.who: Engineering leaders picking a self-hosted coding model benefit; they or a consulting engagement pay.
items.versus: Picking by leaderboard is free but risks a model that ignores your conventions, and no vendor offers perturbation tests on your code.
items.smallest_test: Edit 20 internal tasks MaxxBench-style and run both models; success if the ranking or gap differs meaningfully from the headline benchmark.
items.disconfirm: Rankings on edited internal tasks match the headline benchmark every time.

items.title: Teams self-hosting Qwen3.8-27B can rerun MCP honesty evals on every release
items.connection: DSpine speeds Qwen3.8-27B decoding on agent replays, and MCPHallu is a set of agent replays across real MCP servers built to trigger false-success failures.
items.context: eval suites are usually run once at launch because repeated runs cost too much
chain: DSpine's draft model gives about 2.3x to 3.2x throughput on Qwen3.8-27B agent replays under SGLang.
MCPHallu's 358 tasks across 36 real MCP servers are exactly that kind of replay workload, so a full pass gets cheaper and faster.
A cheap full pass can run in CI on every prompt, tool, or server change, not only at model selection.
Product teams can then report a regression in "admits impossible task" behavior before users see false success messages.
items.who: Teams shipping MCP agents on open models benefit; the product or platform team pays for the GPU time.
items.versus: Running the suite at default speed makes it a quarterly event, and hosted eval services do not run your own MCP servers.
items.smallest_test: Run the MCPHallu suite on Qwen3.8-27B in SGLang with and without DSpine; success if wall-clock time drops at least 2x with matching pass and fail labels on every task.
items.disconfirm: Speculative decoding changes which tasks the agent admits are impossible, or the speedup falls well below 2x on these tasks.

HeteroFold can pass a compressed KV cache to a model from a different family so the receiving model skips million-token prefill entirely.

Memdoor's team workflow supplies a coordinated coding use case for the same Qwen3.8-27B model whose decoding DSpine accelerates.

A dedicated local memory-writer model can implement the deciding-what-to-remember step the design describes.
Builders can apply Anthropic's design reference for organizing memory and correcting mistakes to an open-source memory layer that updates from experience.
The downloadable coding model supplies a concrete target for checking instruction sensitivity beyond its vendor-reported coding score.
